papers.title: Critical Robin Problems on Manifolds with Noncompact Boundary
papers.summary: We work on connected, noncompact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds $(\mathcal{M}, g), n \geq 3$, that are complete with respect to $d_g$ and have noncompact boundary and bounded geometry. We study the existence of positive solutions in $C^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M}) \cap L^{\infty}(\mathcal{M})$ to the Yamabe problem: $$ \left\{\begin{aligned} -Δ_g u+\frac{n-2}{4(n-1)} R_g u & =\mathscr{C}_0 u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} \quad \text { in } \mathcal{M}, \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial ν}+\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)} H_g u & =\mathscr{C}_1 u^{\frac{n}{n-2}} \quad \text { on } \partial \mathcal{M}, \end{aligned}\right. $$ where $\mathscr{C}_0=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}), \mathscr{C}_1=Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}) \mathscr{C} \bar{d}^{\frac{2}{n-2}}$, the parameter $\mathscr{C} \geq 0$ is fixed, and $$ Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M}):=\inf _{u \in C_c^{\infty}(\mathcal{M}) \backslash\{0\}} \frac{E_g(u)}{\left(\|u\|_{L^{2^*}(\mathcal{M})}^{2^*}+\mathscr{C}\|u\|_{L^{2^{\#}}(\partial \mathcal{M})}^{2^*}\right)^{2 / 2^*}} . $$ Here $E_g$ is the associated quadratic energy. We assume $Y_{\mathscr{C}}(\mathcal{M})<Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})$ and $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}(\mathcal{M})>0$, where $Y_{\mathscr{C}, \infty}$ is the corresponding variational level at infinity. We approach this problem using nonnegative solutions $u_j \in W_{\partial}^{1,2}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j)\right), j \in \mathbb{N}, j \geq j_0$, for which we prove that $$ \sup _{j \geq j_0}\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^{\infty}\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j-1)\right)}<\infty . $$ For $\mathscr{C}>0$, we also prove that, along a subsequence, $\left\|u_j\right\|_{L^2{ }_{\left(B_g(\mathcal{O}, j) \cap \partial \mathcal{M}\right)}} \rightarrow \bar{d}$, with $0<\bar{d} \leq \mathscr{C}^{-1 / 2^*}$. For $\mathscr{C}=0$, we set $\bar{d}=0$.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness of the $2$D Euler Evolutions with $L^1\cap L^p$ Vorticity
papers.summary: For each prescribed $1<p<\infty$, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\cap L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)$ that admits two distinct evolutions under the unforced two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation on $[0,1]$. Both vorticities are strongly continuous in $L^1\cap L^p$ and are transported exactly by their respective almost-everywhere invertible, measure-preserving regular Lagrangian flows. The construction couples unstable four-vortex configurations across increasingly small spatial scales, realizing them through concentrated signed vortex patches. At each finite cutoff, a prepared reference evolution remains close to rotating configurations, while a second evolution differs initially only at the finest scale. In the second evolution, the finest configuration consists of separating dipoles whose remote strain activates the instability of the next larger configuration. This process propagates through successive scales with summable transition times. As the cutoff tends to infinity, the two families of initial data converge strongly, along a subsequence, to the same datum, while a nonzero difference survives at a fixed larger scale and is detected by a fixed smooth observable at a positive limiting time. Quantitative concentration and relative comparison estimates establish this cascade for exact Euler patch solutions. Strong compactness through inverse-flow stability then preserves both exact vorticity transport and the positive-time distinction between the two limiting evolutions. The initial datum and construction parameters may depend on $p$.

papers.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in $2$D Euler Equations
papers.summary: We establish a sharp uniqueness--nonuniqueness criterion for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations within a class of stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices. Let $Θ$ be any finite nondecreasing envelope for the vorticity $L^p$ norms, and set $I_Θ=\int_{p_0}^\infty Θ(p)^{-1}\,dp$. If $I_Θ=\infty$, every array in the corresponding class admits a unique Euler evolution, even among bounded energy-admissible weak velocity solutions. If $I_Θ<\infty$, there exists a compactly supported array in the same class admitting two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions from the same initial datum. The criterion holds for arbitrary nondecreasing envelopes $Θ$.

papers.title: Sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with Hörmander operators
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the Cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal L u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal L=\sum_{j=1}^mX_j^2$ is a homogeneous Hörmander sum of squares on $\mathbb R^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. Diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. We prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T)=\int_0^Th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $T_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{H}_{p,h}(T_\varepsilon)\le C\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. Our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a Gaussian-envelope energy and an ODE cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. The result contains the Euclidean, Heisenberg, Carnot and Grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. We also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness of Landau Equation in Bounded Domains
papers.summary: We prove global well-posedness of the Landau equation near a Maxwellian in bounded $C^3$ domains with in-flow or diffuse-reflection boundary conditions for $-3\leqγ\leq1$, including Coulomb interactions. Small compatible Gaussian perturbations generate global strong solutions, with uniqueness and continuous dependence among weak solutions. The proof combines energy estimates, the comparison principle, interior and weighted boundary estimates for velocity derivatives up to second order, and a logarithmic estimate for solution difference.

papers.title: On the existence of minimizers for the generalized liquid drop model
papers.summary: We consider a broad class of generalized liquid drop models in which a perimeter term competes with repulsive nonlocal interactions with finite first moments. For all such kernels satisfying the natural physical assumption of reflection positivity we show existence of minimizers for all masses, in the (super-)critical regime. Moreover, in the subcritical regime we give the first quantitative estimate of the range of masses for which existence holds, which converges to the whole positive real line as one approaches the critical regime. This result builds on the nonlocal curvature approach introduced and developed in the periodic setting in \cite{dr24}.

papers.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
papers.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.

papers.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
papers.summary: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation for repulsive Vlasov--Riesz--Fokker--Planck (VRFP) equations on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unregularized interaction potentials with singularity $|x|^{-s}$, $0<s<d/2$. On every finite time interval on which the limiting classical solution satisfies the stated regularity assumptions, the particle marginals with a product initial law converge at an algebraic rate in the particle number, with constants growing at most exponentially in the marginal order. For the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$, a weighted $C^m$ initial probability density, $m\ge3$, with Gaussian velocity decay and polynomial spatial decay of order $M>3$ gives convergence to the global classical solution on every finite time interval. The proof combines conditioning of the initial product law with weighted BBGKY estimates. A decomposition of the potential and a bounded modification of the far-field force yield weighted bounds growing geometrically in the marginal order on the prescribed interval. A centered second-moment estimate permits summation of the error hierarchy, and a synchronous coupling transfers the estimate to the original dynamics.

papers.title: Sharp $L^2$ stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
papers.summary: We establish quantitative stability for radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the Minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. Here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. For the $L^2$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. We also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $L^2$-Heisenberg inequality, respectively. For $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(N-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $L^p$-Heisenberg inequalities. As a byproduct, we establish weighted $L^p$-Poincaré inequalities for Gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

papers.title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
papers.summary: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
papers.summary: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $γ\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $γ$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
papers.summary: At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-Δu=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].

papers.title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.summary: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.

papers.title: Second variation of the fractional torsion energy and linear stability of the ball
papers.summary: We compute the second shape derivative of the fractional torsion. It is an explicit quadratic form on the boundary, which involves a Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator for half-harmonic functions blowing up at the boundary. We deduce an explicit formula for volume preserving variations on the ball and show that as in the local case, the shape Hessian is negative and coercive in \(H^{1/2}\) modulo translations.

papers.title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
papers.summary: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.

papers.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
papers.summary: We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calderón-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(σ)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $σ$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

papers.title: Topological defect trains excited by a boundary discontinuity in the two-dimensional complex Ginzburg-Landau equation
papers.summary: With numerical simulations of the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation in a two-dimensional space, we find that a stationary but non-zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a discontinuity can drive a periodic train of evenly spaced topological defects that drift along and in proximity to the boundary.

papers.title: $γ$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
papers.summary: Let $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_Σ:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrowγ(L^2(Σ),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_Σ:γ(L^2(Σ),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schrödinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

papers.title: A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
papers.summary: We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Ampère measure
papers.summary: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!μ$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $μ\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $μ$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Ampère measures of Hölder continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields Hölder continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a Hölder continuous periodic function.

papers.title: The Hénon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent
papers.summary: We consider the Dirichlet problem $-Δu=|x|^αu^p$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $α>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_α=\frac{N+2+2α}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_α$, provided $Ω$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.

papers.title: Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data
papers.summary: We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{σ+λ-n}-$regularity of solutions when $σ+λ-n\neq1$, where $σ\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $λ\in(n-σ,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $σ+λ-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.

papers.title: Variational characterization of principal eigenvalues for a general class of linear weighted BVP's under mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type
papers.summary: The main goal of this paper is to characterize the existence of principal eigenvalues of $$ \left \{ \begin{array}{ll} -\mathrm{div}\left(A\nabla u\right) +qu=λm u \quad & \hbox{in} \;\; Ω,\\[1ex] \mathscr{B} u = 0 \quad & \hbox{on} \;\; \partial Ω, \end{array} \right. $$ where $m\in L^\infty(Ω)$ satisfies some of the conditions (A1)-(A3) below, as well as to deliver their variational characterizations whenever they exist. As we are dealing with general boundary operators of mixed non-classical type, in the general setting of this paper our results are far more general than all existing results. The case when $m$ satisfies (A2) has not been previously explored in the literature.

papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
papers.summary: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate a matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem whose solution provides a reconstruction formula for the solution of the original Cauchy problem.

papers.title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
papers.summary: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_θ}\), where \(A_θ\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. For time-dependent forcing terms, a direct kernel-based evaluation requires repeated quadrature over delayed kernel evaluations. To address this computational bottleneck, we derive a latent-first reformulation of the source term: the forcing field is projected onto the kernel-induced latent space, where its accumulated effect is represented as the solution of a forced linear latent dynamical system. For a fixed learned kernel, this reformulation is exact. The resulting system can then be integrated using a \(φ_1\)-based exponential integrator, yielding a source-evaluation path that is structurally aligned with the learned latent propagator. The resulting framework combines geometry- and physics-conditioned low-rank kernel factorization with alternative source-evaluation paths based on either explicit Duhamel quadrature or latent exponential integration. Dissipativity constraints on the latent generator and identity-preserving corrections near the initial time are optional architectural components. Numerical experiments on advection-iffusion-reaction (ADR) problems compare the non-ODE and semigroup-aware formulations, evaluate the quadrature and \(φ_1\) source paths, and assess predictive accuracy and computational cost.
